c2-09.q: Which sentence renders Covadonga's thought as free indirect speech?
options: Covadonga pensó que quizá la tía había tenido un hijo.
Covadonga se preguntó si la tía había tenido un hijo.
Covadonga dijo: «¿Ha tenido un hijo la tía?»
c2-09.why: Free indirect speech drops the verb of thinking and lets the character's own questions and exclamations appear inside the narration.

c2-09.q: When Nina says «ven, guapina, que te hago un cafetín», what do the suffixes mainly express?
options: That the coffee is very small
That the child is younger than six
Affection and a regional Asturian voice
c2-09.why: Asturian -ín/-ina here marks tenderness and local identity, not size.

c2-09.q: Complete: «La caja estaba tan escondida que Covadonga por poco ___ al contenedor.»
c2-09.why: Por poco for a near miss in the past normally takes the present indicative (por poco la tira); the subjunctive and conditional are wrong.

c2-09.q: In «La que fuera la casa de ambos era ahora un edificio de oficinas», fuera means:
c2-09.why: In literary register the -ra form can carry pluperfect indicative value: la que fuera = la que había sido.

c2-09.q: Complete: «Por poco que ___ de ruso, aquella palabra la entendió.»
c2-09.why: Por poco que ('however little') is concessive and takes the subjunctive; past narration requires the imperfect subjunctive.

c2-09.q: Find the mistake: «Hubo terminado la cinta y la puso otra vez.»
options: The verb puso should be ponía
The pretérito anterior needs a time conjunction: Apenas hubo terminado…
c2-09.why: The pretérito anterior is only used after apenas, cuando, en cuanto, no bien, etc., never on its own.

c2-09.q: Galina lives in «un pisucho de La Calzada». What does -ucho add?
options: A mildly disparaging but affectionate tone
A neutral sense of small size
That the flat belongs to someone else
c2-09.why: -ucho downgrades with a touch of fondness or self-irony; it is a stance, not a measurement.

c2-09.q: Choose the best free indirect version of: Covadonga se preguntó si la tía había dejado al niño allí.
options: ¿Lo había dejado allí, con su padre, con quien fuera?
Covadonga se preguntó que si lo dejaba allí.
c2-09.why: Free indirect speech keeps third person and past tenses but drops the reporting verb and keeps the question form.

c2-10.topic: Legal register and the future subjunctive
c2-10.q: Complete the legal formula: «Si la parte obligada no lo ___ en el plazo de quince días, quedará sin efecto el acuerdo.»
c2-10.why: Legal hypotheticals keep the future subjunctive (hiciere), built on the stem of hicieron.

c2-10.q: Which is a correct absolute construction?
c2-10.why: The participle comes first and agrees with its own subject: firmada la carta.

c2-10.topic: Mood for stance: aunque, el hecho de que, como
c2-10.q: Zoila says «Aunque la canción sea un éxito en medio mundo, la voz es de don Anselmo». Why the subjunctive, if the song really is a hit?
options: Because she grants the fact but treats it as irrelevant to her argument
Because aunque always takes the subjunctive
Because she doubts that it is a hit
Because the sentence is about the future
c2-10.why: Aunque + subjunctive can concede a known fact while dismissing its weight.

c2-10.topic: Rhetorical devices: anaphora, rhetorical questions, tricolon
c2-10.q: «Pueden decir que…; pueden decir que…; pueden decir que…» is an example of:
c2-10.why: Anaphora is the repetition of the same opening in successive clauses.

c2-10.topic: Mood for stance: aunque, el hecho de que, como
c2-10.q: What does «Como no lo corrijan antes del lunes, le mando otra carta notarial» mean?
options: If they don't correct it before Monday, I'll send another letter.
Since they haven't corrected it, I'll send a letter.
As they corrected it on Monday, I sent a letter.
However they correct it, I'll send a letter.
c2-10.why: Como + subjunctive at the start of a sentence is a conditional warning; with the indicative it would mean 'since'.

c2-10.topic: Legal register and the future subjunctive
c2-10.q: Rewrite in everyday Spanish: «Quien alegare derechos deberá acreditarlos.»
c2-10.why: Outside legal register the future subjunctive is replaced by the present subjunctive after quien with future reference.

c2-10.q: Choose the register-appropriate opening for a court report: «___, el juez levantó la sesión.»
options: Cuando ya habían acabado con lo de los testigos
Después de oír a los testigos ellos
c2-10.why: An absolute participle clause (oídos los testigos) is the compact, formal choice for procedural narration.

c2-10.topic: Rhetorical devices: anaphora, rhetorical questions, tricolon
c2-10.q: Which ending keeps the tricolon parallel? «No pedimos caridad; pedimos un nombre, una firma y ___.»
options: que nos paguen lo que deben
c2-10.why: A tricolon keeps the same grammatical shape: three noun phrases (un nombre, una firma, una deuda saldada).

c2-01.q: Reyes ends: «Una jueza que se condena a sí misma y sale ovacionada: no está nada mal para un viernes.» What does she really mean?
options: The evening was only moderately successful.
She is disappointed that the jury did not vote.
She is delighted, but says so with dry understatement.
Fridays are usually bad nights at the Falla.
c2-01.why: No está nada mal is litotes: denying a negative to express strong approval in a dry, ironic tone.

c2-01.q: Curro says «Cría fama…» and stops. How does Inma correctly complete the proverb?
c2-01.why: The full proverb is Cría fama y échate a dormir: once you have a reputation, it sticks.

c2-01.topic: Mood for stance: aunque, el hecho de que, como
c2-01.q: Reyes accepts that Fali is a rogue but says it is irrelevant. Complete: «Aunque Fali ___ un sinvergüenza, esta vez no ha robado nada.»
c2-01.why: Aunque + subjunctive presents a known fact as irrelevant to the conclusion: aunque sea.

c2-01.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
c2-01.q: Complete Curro's protest: «¡Ni que ___ la primera vez que Fali nos levanta un chiste!»
c2-01.why: The formula ¡Ni que…! takes the past subjunctive, here the imperfect: ni que fuera.

c2-01.topic: Mood for stance: aunque, el hecho de que, como
c2-01.q: Which sentence uses como to express a warning rather than a cause?
options: Como actuábamos el viernes, quedaban treinta y seis horas.
Como era martes, el teatro estaba medio vacío.
Como el jurado tenga el mismo sentido del humor que yo, no pasamos.
Como Benito grababa todo, había cientos de cintas.
c2-01.why: Como + subjunctive at the start of a sentence is a threat or condition; como + indicative gives a cause.

c2-01.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
options: No era, que digamos, una perspectiva alegre.
Sea como sea, el cuplé hay que cambiarlo.
Que yo sé, nadie grabó el ensayo.
Como quien no quiere la cosa, se sentó al fondo.
c2-01.why: The formula is que yo sepa, always with the subjunctive.

c2-01.q: Which choice keeps Reyes's ironic register when she describes her own costume idea?
options: Un tipo que propuse yo, porque soy la mejor.
Un tipo que propuso otra persona.
Un tipo que, con modestia ejemplar, propuse yo.
Un tipo que, por desgracia, propuse yo.
c2-01.why: Con modestia ejemplar is mock praise: it pretends to be modest while openly claiming credit.

c2-01.q: Fali answers «En casa del herrero…» with «…cuchillo de palo. Y en la de la jueza, plagio.» What is he doing with the proverb?
options: Completing it and then twisting it into an ironic joke about Reyes.
Replacing it with a different proverb with the same meaning.
c2-01.why: He finishes the refrán as expected and then adds a new, parallel ending aimed at Reyes, a typical ironic twist.

c2-02.q: «¿Qué se creía el Cholo? ¿Que iba a dejar que cualquiera hurgara en lo único que le quedaba del viejo?» Whose questions are these?
options: Obdulio's thoughts, inside the third-person narration.
c2-02.why: There is no verb of saying, but the questions, the anger and the word el viejo belong to Obdulio: this is free indirect speech.

c2-02.q: In «¿La lonja? Rajada de punta a punta», which verb is understood?
c2-02.why: The fragment describes the state of the drumhead, so the missing verb is estar: estaba rajada.

c2-02.q: Complete with the topic first: «Aquel tambor ___ había hecho su padre en el patio del Mediomundo.»
c2-02.why: A fronted direct object must be repeated by a clitic that agrees with it: aquel tambor → lo.

c2-02.q: Before the parade the drums are brought to the fire «para templar los cueros». What does templar mean here?
options: To tune the drumheads by heating them.
To clean the drums with smoke.
To soften the leather so it can be folded.
c2-02.why: In candombe, templar is to tune the drum, traditionally by heating the hide over a street fire.

c2-02.q: Which sentence shows Rioplatense clitic doubling with the object left in its normal position?
options: Conocí a tu viejo tocando ese tambor.
Lo conocí a tu viejo tocando ese tambor.
A tu viejo lo conocí tocando ese tambor.
Tu viejo me conoció tocando ese tambor.
c2-02.why: In lo conocí a tu viejo the pronoun doubles an object that stays after the verb, typical of River Plate speech; option B is left dislocation.

c2-02.q: Which is the full sentence behind «Cuero nuevo, aro nuevo. El sonido, el de siempre»?
options: Había un cuero nuevo y quería un aro nuevo, y el sonido siempre era así.
Le pusieron cuero nuevo y aro nuevo, pero el sonido era el de siempre.
Compraron un cuero y un aro para cambiar el sonido.
El cuero nuevo sonaba como un aro nuevo.
c2-02.why: The fragments drop the verbs (pusieron, era); the comma after el sonido replaces era.

c2-02.q: Turn Obdulio's direct thought «¿Retirarme yo? Mañana llevaré el tambor al taller» into free indirect speech.
options: Obdulio pensó que no se retiraría y que mañana llevará el tambor.
¿Retirarme yo?, pensó él. Mañana llevaré el tambor al taller.
¿Retirarse? ¿Él? Mañana llevaría el tambor al taller.
Obdulio dijo: «¿Retirarse él? Mañana llevaría el tambor al taller».
c2-02.why: Free indirect speech keeps the question and mañana but shifts to the third person and the past (llevaría), without a verb of saying.

c2-02.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three drums of the candombe cuerda?
c2-02.why: The cuerda is chico, repique and piano; the gramillero is a dancing character, an old herb doctor.

c2-03.q: Anacleto says: «Courtney, this is not a pancake: es un yaniqueque». Why does he switch to Spanish halfway?
options: Because he forgets the English word for it
To meet her in English but insist on the Spanish name of a dish that is part of his identity
Because English has no present tense of ser
Because yaniqueque is a rude word in English
c2-03.why: The switch marks identity: he accommodates her language but keeps his food's own name.

c2-03.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
c2-03.q: Complete: «¿Que mi comida lo adelgaza? ¡Ni que le ___ sirviendo agua!»
c2-03.why: ¡Ni que…! takes the past subjunctive (here the imperfect), even about the present.

c2-03.q: Which sentence means 'I nearly dropped the pot'?
options: Por poco se me cae el caldero.
Por poco que se me cayera el caldero.
Por poco se me caiga el caldero.
Con lo que se me cae el caldero.
c2-03.why: A near miss in the past uses por poco + present indicative.

c2-03.q: Anacleto says Courtney «no tiene un pelo de tonta». What does he mean?
options: She is not clever at all
c2-03.why: Litotes: denying the opposite (not a hair of a fool) affirms that she is sharp.

c2-03.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
options: Que yo sé, aquí nadie se ha muerto de un domplín.
No era muy científico que digamos.
Se puso de su lado como quien no quiere la cosa.
c2-03.why: The fixed formula is que yo sepa, with the subjunctive.

c2-03.q: «Por poco que comiera, con mis raciones tendría que mantener el peso.» What does por poco que mean here?
c2-03.why: Por poco que + subjunctive is concessive: 'however little'.

c2-03.q: Which word is a loan fully adapted to Spanish, not a code-switch?
c2-03.why: Domplín (from dumpling) has Spanish spelling, stress and plural (domplines); the others stay English.

c2-03.q: Choose the ironic register: Anacleto wants to say Courtney lectured him although he is the expert.
options: La nutricionista me explicó la proteína con mucha claridad.
La nutricionista, con modestia ejemplar, le explicó la proteína a un hombre que lleva treinta años cocinando para atletas.
La nutricionista no sabía nada de proteína.
La nutricionista me explicó la proteína y yo aprendí mucho.
c2-03.why: Praise that the context contradicts (modestia ejemplar) is the ironic choice; the others are literal.

c2-04.q: Complete in standard Spanish: «Los planos ___ habían dibujado sobre una foto aérea vieja.»
c2-04.why: A fronted direct object needs a copy pronoun that agrees: los planos → los.

c2-04.q: Doña Jacinta says: «¡Qué obrita la de la Gobernación!» What does the diminutive express?
options: That the project is very small
Irony: she belittles a large project
c2-04.why: Applied to a big public work, -ita is ironic, not about size.

c2-04.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
c2-04.q: «¡Había sido verdad lo del cementerio!» What does había sido express here?
options: Sudden discovery: it was true all along
An event before another past event
c2-04.why: This is the Andean mirative pluperfect, which marks surprise at a new realisation.

c2-04.topic: Rhetorical devices: anaphora, rhetorical questions, tricolon
c2-04.q: «No vine a pedir permiso, no vine a pedir perdón: vine a rendir cuentas.» Which device is the repeated «no vine a…»?
c2-04.why: Anaphora repeats the opening words of successive clauses.

options: La copla la oyó la primera noche.
A doña Jacinta yo nunca la he oído cantar nada ajeno.
c2-04.why: A fronted direct object needs its copy pronoun: A mi papá lo enterraron ahí.

c2-04.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
c2-04.q: Simona writes a formal technical report. Which way of marking hearsay fits that register?
options: Dizque el consultor no visitó la obra.
Según parece, el consultor no visitó la obra.
El consultor no visitó la obra, dice.
¡El consultor no había visitado la obra!
c2-04.why: Según parece is the neutral written option; dizque and final dice are colloquial.

c2-04.q: In the last copla doña Jacinta sings ingeniera, not ingenierita. What does the change signal?
options: Respect: she no longer belittles Simona
c2-04.why: Dropping the belittling diminutive is itself a sign of respect.

c2-04.topic: Rhetorical devices: anaphora, rhetorical questions, tricolon
c2-04.q: Which version keeps the tricolon parallel?
options: para los que pasan, los que se quedan y quienes ya murieron
para quienes pasan, para el que se queda y por los muertos
para los que pasan y se quedan, además de los muertos
para los que pasan, para los que se quedan y para los que ya no están
c2-04.why: A tricolon repeats the same frame three times; only the last option keeps para los que… throughout.

c2-05.q: A reporter has not confirmed the theft. Complete: «Según fuentes policiales, la vasija ___ del sitio durante la noche.»
c2-05.why: Habría + participle reports unconfirmed past information; fue and había sido state it as fact, and the subjunctive has no trigger here.

c2-05.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
c2-05.q: Complete: «A lo mejor ___ una réplica, don Nefta.»
c2-05.why: A lo mejor always takes the indicative, unlike quizá and tal vez.

c2-05.q: Which sentence is a verbless fragment in which the reader recovers 'estaba'?
c2-05.why: The comma stands for the missing verb (La olla, perfecta = the pot was perfect); without it, la olla perfecta is just a noun phrase.

c2-05.q: Complete in report style: «Cabe la posibilidad de que ___ otras réplicas en circulación.»
c2-05.why: Cabe la posibilidad de que presents an open possibility, so it takes the subjunctive: existan.

c2-05.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
c2-05.q: Neftalí thinks the paper is probably right. Which sentence shows that stance?
options: A lo mejor tenga razón el periódico.
c2-05.why: Quizá with the indicative signals a real, fairly likely possibility; the subjunctive makes it more remote, and a lo mejor never takes the subjunctive.

c2-05.q: Find the mistake in this correction notice: «La pieza habría sido una réplica de fabricación reciente, según el informe técnico. Lamentamos el error.»
options: Habría sido should be es: a correction states the confirmed fact
c2-05.why: A correction retracts the rumour, so it uses the indicative (la pieza es una réplica); keeping the conditional would still sound unconfirmed.

c2-05.q: Which version belongs in Yesenia's official report?
options: No se constatan alteraciones recientes en la estratigrafía.
Yo creo que nadie ha tocado la tierra.
Aquí no ha escarbado nadie, se lo juro.
Me parece que no hay nada raro en las capas.
c2-05.why: Impersonal se constata with a technical noun keeps the writer out of the claim, as academic register requires; the others are personal speech.

c2-05.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
c2-05.q: Neftalí thinks the hope is unlikely to come true. Complete: «Ojalá ___ tan fácil.»
c2-05.why: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a hope seen as unlikely or contrary to fact; ojalá sea would be a hope that may well come true.

c2-06.q: A press bulletin does not want to vouch for the date. Complete: «El pueblo ___ en 1609, de acuerdo con fuentes municipales.»
c2-06.why: Habría + participle presents a past claim as unconfirmed and attributed to a source; fue and había sido state it as fact.

c2-06.q: In «Don Fidencio, quien fuera su maestro de jarana», what does fuera mean?
c2-06.why: In literary relative clauses the -ra form works as a pluperfect indicative: quien fuera = who had (once) been.

c2-06.topic: Concessive and conjectural future and conditional
c2-06.q: Which sentence concedes a point about the past before an objection?
options: Será príncipe cuando lo diga la placa.
Sería príncipe o no, pero cimarrón lo fue.
c2-06.why: The conditional sería concedes a possibility about the past (prince or not) before pero introduces what is certain.

c2-06.q: Don Fidencio says only «No por mucho madrugar…». What is he telling Ruperto?
options: Get up earlier tomorrow and go to the town hall
He has forgotten the rest of the proverb
Early risers always get what they want
Don't rush: hurrying won't make things happen sooner
c2-06.why: The truncated proverb (no por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano) tells Ruperto not to rush; the listener completes it.

c2-06.q: Find the mistake: «Ruperto hubo leído el borrador y pidió una pluma roja.»
options: el borrador should be al borrador
hubo leído needs a time connector such as apenas or no bien
c2-06.why: The pretérito anterior is only used after connectors like apenas, no bien, una vez que: Apenas hubo leído el borrador, pidió…

c2-06.topic: Concessive and conjectural future and conditional
c2-06.q: What does «Tendrá razón el video en lo del orgullo; en las fechas, no» mean?
options: The video will be right about the pride in the future.
The video should be right about the pride.
The video may well be right about the pride, but not about the dates.
The video was right about everything.
c2-06.why: The concessive future grants a point about the present (may well be right) before rejecting another; it is not a real future.

c2-06.q: Ruperto rewrites the plaque so the bronze states only documented facts. Which sentence fits the final plaque?
options: Yanga habría fundado el pueblo en 1609.
El pueblo habría sido reconocido como libre.
Yanga habría resistido la campaña de 1609.
El pueblo lleva su nombre desde 1932.
c2-06.why: A text that commits to its facts uses the indicative; the conditional of rumour signals that the writer does not vouch for the claim.

c2-06.q: Which is a twisted proverb used for irony?
options: Cada quien habla de la feria según le va en ella.
No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano.
Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho, y del hecho a la placa, más todavía.
c2-06.why: Adding an unexpected ending (y del hecho a la placa…) twists the proverb for an ironic point; the others are quoted whole or truncated.

c2-07.topic: Legal register and the future subjunctive
c2-07.q: Complete the warning read to witnesses: «Quien ___ a la verdad en su declaración incurrirá en falso testimonio.»
c2-07.why: Legal formulas keep the future subjunctive (faltare) in an open, hypothetical relative clause; everyday Spanish would say quien falte.

c2-07.q: Complete: «___ el acta de la declaración policial, la presidenta preguntó a la testigo si la ratificaba.»
c2-07.why: In an absolute construction the participle agrees with its own subject, acta, which is feminine even though it takes el.

c2-07.q: In ña Gumersinda's «Vení-na un ratito, sentate conmigo», what does -na add to the command?
options: It turns the command into a question
It puts the command in the past
It softens the request and makes it friendlier
It makes the order more urgent and abrupt
c2-07.why: The Guaraní particle -na, attached to Spanish imperatives in Paraguay, softens a request, like 'won't you' or 'please'.

c2-07.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
c2-07.q: The witness said «Derlis ndaje oĩ va'ekue kokue rembe'ýpe». Which Spanish version is faithful?
options: Vi a Derlis al borde de la chacra.
Derlis tiene que haber estado al borde de la chacra.
Dicen que Derlis estaba al borde de la chacra.
Juro que Derlis estaba al borde de la chacra.
c2-07.why: Ndaje is a reportative: the speaker repeats what others say, so dicen que keeps the source; vi or juro turn hearsay into eyewitness evidence.

c2-07.topic: Legal register and the future subjunctive
c2-07.q: Which sentence uses the future subjunctive correctly in legal register?
options: Cuando se hiciere ayer la lectura, el juez habló.
Si así no se hará, se dejará constancia en el acta.
Si así no se hiciere, se dejare constancia en el acta.
Si así no se hiciere, se dejará constancia en el acta.
c2-07.why: The -re form goes only in the hypothetical si or relative clause; the main clause takes the future indicative, and it never refers to past events.

c2-07.q: Rewrite «Cuando el muchacho fue absuelto, la sala se vació» as an absolute construction.
options: Absolviendo el muchacho, la sala se vació.
Absuelta al muchacho, la sala se vació.
El muchacho absuelto, la sala lo vació.
Absuelto el muchacho, la sala se vació.
c2-07.why: Participle first, agreeing with its own subject (absuelto el muchacho), then the main clause; a gerund would wrongly make la sala the one acquitting.

c2-07.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
c2-07.q: Perla exclaims «¡Había sido cierto lo de la miel!». What does había sido express here?
options: Something that was true before but is no longer true
A rumour she still does not believe
Surprise at a fact she has only just discovered
An event that happened before another past event
c2-07.why: In Paraguayan and Andean Spanish this mirative pluperfect marks sudden discovery: 'so it was true!'.

c2-07.q: Ña Gumersinda's answer ends with a Paraguayan «luego». What does it mean in that position?
c2-07.why: Under Guaraní influence, sentence-final luego in Paraguay is an emphatic particle, not the time adverb 'later'.

c2-08.q: How do you say 'the children' in Palenquero?
c2-08.why: Palenquero marks the plural with the particle ma before the noun, and the noun itself does not change.

c2-08.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
c2-08.q: Complete Dorina's reply: «A lo mejor solo ___ delirando.»
c2-08.why: A lo mejor always takes the indicative, unlike quizá and tal vez.

c2-08.topic: Concessive and conjectural future and conditional
c2-08.q: Which form gives the concessive meaning 'He may be very stubborn, but he's no fool'? «___ su tío muy terco, pero no es tonto.»
c2-08.why: The future of conjecture followed by pero concedes a point (será terco) before contradicting it; es would simply state a fact.

c2-08.q: Complete the hedged sentence: «Cabe la posibilidad de que se ___ de un préstamo léxico del kikongo.»
c2-08.why: Cabe la posibilidad de que expresses possibility, so it takes the subjunctive: se trate.

c2-08.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
options: A lo mejor alguien más joven acepta el puesto.
A lo mejor alguien más joven acepte el puesto.
Tal vez no lo conteste nunca.
c2-08.why: A lo mejor never takes the subjunctive; quizá and tal vez can take either mood.

c2-08.topic: Concessive and conjectural future and conditional
c2-08.q: In past narration, «Tendría sus razones el tío, pensó, pero también ella tenía las suyas» means:
options: Her uncle would have reasons in the future.
Her uncle had to explain his reasons.
Her uncle should have given his reasons.
Her uncle may have had his reasons, but she had hers too.
c2-08.why: Here the conditional is conjectural and concessive about the past: 'he may have had his reasons, but...'.

c2-08.q: Which sentence belongs in Dorina's abstract rather than in a conversation?
options: Los datos apuntan a un uso restringido al ámbito del kuagro.
Yo creo que la palabra viene del kikongo, ¿sabes?
A lo mejor la abuela se lo inventó, ¿no?
Mi tío dice que eso no es pa' la universidad.
c2-08.why: Academic prose is impersonal and hedged, with data as the subject (los datos apuntan a) and no yo, tags or colloquial forms.

c2-08.q: In «Ma Petrona» and «ma moná», the word ma...
options: is the plural marker in both
is a respectful title before a name in the first, and a plural marker before a noun in the second
is a Spanish article in both
c2-08.why: The story distinguishes the title Ma before an older woman's name from the Palenquero plural particle ma.
